artworks.title: Base with Reliefs of the Birth of Zeus
artworks.description: Capitoline statue base: Curetes clash shields while the infant Zeus is nursed in the Cretan cave — the Dictaean childhood Adrasteia and Ida share with Amalthea in the nurse tradition. Musei Capitolini, Rome.

artworks.title: Rhea Presents the Swaddled Stone to Cronus (relief)
artworks.description: The trick that sends Zeus to Crete: Rhea hands Cronus the swaddled stone so the child can be raised by the mountain nurses — Adrasteia's Dictaean charge begins where this relief ends.

popCulture.title: Adrasteia
popCulture.description: Cretan nymph (daughter of Melisseus in some accounts) entrusted with infant Zeus beside Ida — later overlapped with Nemesis/Inescapable as a mountain goddess.

popCulture.title: Curetes
popCulture.description: The armed dancers who drowned the infant's cries with their shields — Adrasteia's companions in the cave of Zeus' rearing.

popCulture.title: Rhea (mythology)
popCulture.description: The mother who hid Zeus from Cronus and committed him to the Cretan nurses — Adrasteia's charge begins with Rhea's escape.
